title: Eagles rally to stun Cowboys coming back from 21 points behind
rawText:
Eagles rally to stun Cowboys coming back from 21 points behind
ARLINGTON, Texas — Joe Milton rolled to his left while motioning DeVonta Smith where to go near the end zone, then threw the kind of deep ball the Dallas Cowboys always knew he was capable of when he was playing for them.
That 50-yarder was the first of two long touchdowns for the Philadelphia duo against the quarterback's former team, and the start of quite a comeback.
Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup all last season, threw three touchdowns and ran for another one in a 39-38 win Thursday in his third start for the Eagles, who signed him off the Dallas practice squad on Oct. 16.
"The guy's a rock star. ... True example of being cool, calm, collected, and just keep playing the next play, no matter what the outcome," said Eagles tackle Jordan Mailata, who was then asked about the long TD passes. "We've seen it in practice a couple of times. The oohs and aahs were still there, but not as much. It was just like you know he can get that throw done."
After 50- and 45-yard touchdown passes to Smith, Milton ran 15 yards for a score in the fourth quarter and threw a 24-yard TD to Makai Lemon with 2:10 left before Philadelphia lined up for a 2-point conversion. Milton connected with Smith in the end zone, but a holding call against Mailata wiped out the tying score before another try was broken up at the goal line.
But the Eagles (4-7), who were down 31-10 early in the third quarter, got one more chance after sacking Prescott on fourth-and-1 for a nine-yard loss to their 48 in the final minute. After a couple of short completions to Smith and a pass interference call against Dallas, Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds left.
Milton, signed by the Eagles about the same time they were determining that Jalen Hurts' season was over because of diagnosis of blood clots, completed 21 of 31 passes for a career-best 331 yards.
"You never know when your opportunity is going to come. You never know, when, where, how. The only thing you can do is just prepare yourself," Milton said. "That's just the main thing I did. There wasn't a day where I was in a Cowboys facility and I didn't take notes. I didn't let a day go by where I didn't ask a question. So just being prepared for the moment and I mean, it showed up when it needed to. ... Really trying to hold my emotions in up here. Just thankful for the moment."
While he was sacked five times, and the Cowboys defense had him on the run throughout, Milton made several big plays out of the pocket.
On the 50-yard TD late in the first half, Milton rolled to his left and was in front of the Cowboys sideline when he threw back toward the center of the field — the ball was in the air more than 60 yards before Smith caught it at the goal line. Milton then looked toward the Dallas bench and made some seemingly good-natured gestures with a huge smile on his face.
"Can't even remember doing that, but it was just kind of in a moment," he said.
Then late in the third quarter, while rolling to his right toward his sideline, Milton threw deep to an open Smith, who after the catch had to take only a few steps into the end zone to complete the 45-yard score. Smith had 11 catches for 200 yards.
Milton's quick sprint down the sideline on his touchdown run got the Eagles within 38-30 with 9:09 left.
"He played his butt off. He played really good, made some throws that only he can make," coach Nick Sirianni said. "He played an outstanding game, super composed throughout."
After appearing in four games for Dallas last season, Milton lost his backup role to Sam Howell in training camp this year. But Milton stayed with the Cowboys on their practice squad until getting signed by their NFC East rival.

title: Guarda tus billetes: Ferrari México rechaza pagos en efectivo y depósitos a otras cuentas
rawText:
Ferrari México informó que no recibe pagos en efectivo, con lo que llamó a las personas a no realizar ningún depósito a cuentas distintas para prevenir fraudes.
A través de sus redes sociales, difundieron un comunicado en el que aclararon que, bajo ningún concepto, reciben apartados, anticipos, enganches, liquidaciones, servicios o cualquier otra transacción.
“Ningún colaborador está autorizado para recibir efectivo a nombre de la empresa”, declaró Ferrari, la armadora italiana operada en México por la controladora RIVI S.A de C.V.
Con ello, explicaron que Ferrari México nunca solicitará pagos a cuentas de personas físicas ni de otras empresas, y todos los pagos posibles se deben realizar mediante transferencia o depósito bancario a la cuenta oficial a nombre de la controladora RIVI.
La empresa no informó en el comunicado si el comunicado es con relación a algún caso reciente o si tiene que ver con alguna modificación interna.
Ferrari alerta por posibles fraudes: ¿Qué hacer si recibes una solicitud de pago no oficial?
Si estás interesado en comprar un Ferrari en México, la empresa indica que si recibes una solicitud de pago de una cuenta distinta, o recibiste un mensaje que te genera dudas, no realices el pago y te comuniques directamente con la empresa.
Para ello, puedes contactarles al teléfono 55 55576799 o al correo ferrari@ferrarimexico.com.mx.
La controladora RIVI declaró queno se hace responsable por pagos en efectivo o depósitos y transferencias a cuentas distintas a las oficiales, y tampoco por los daños o pérdidas que podrían afectar a los compradores.
“Agradecemos su comprensión y confianza. Estas medidas tienen como único objetivo ”proteger su patrimonio y garantizar la seguridad de cada operación".
Ferrari México tiene en su página web los modelos a la venta que ofrece como dealer oficial, además de los requisitos para apartar un modelos y, en ciertos casos, precios de cada una de las unidades.

title: Powerful Thanksgiving Day storm causes flooding, power outages
rawText:
Powerful Thanksgiving Day storm brings flooding, power outages to Northeast, Midwest
A Thanksgiving storm brought foul weather to the East Coast and Midwest on Thursday, causing major power outages, disrupting holiday travel and prompting the historic postponement of New York City's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
More than 800,000 customers were without power Thursday night across the Midwest and Northeast, according to the utility tracking website PowerOutage.us. Of those, more than 170,000 customers were without electricity in Pennsylvania, along with more than 170,000 in New Jersey and 130,000 in Maryland.
More than 2,500 flights to or from U.S. destinations were delayed Thursday, and more than 460 were canceled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.
The storm hammered sections of the East Coast with torrential rain, high winds and flooding. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency, declared by Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Wednesday night, as were parts of New York, following a declaration from Gov. Kathy Hochul. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic to southern New England.
Stormy weather creates havoc in New York City
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday morning that two people had to be rescued from their cars because of flooding. He cautioned people not to attempt to walk, bike or drive through flooded areas.
"We want to remind everyone to stay safe and there is no destination worth your safety," Mamdani said.
The New York City Emergency Management agency reported that the city received 1.5 to 2 inches of rain on Thanksgiving, with some parts seeing up to 3 inches. High tides brought flooding to the city's coastal areas, including portions of Staten Island and Long Island.
Central Park saw wind gusts higher than 30 mph, the agency said, while LaGuardia Airport recorded winds of 56 mph. Several scaffolding structures collapsed in the wind, with no injuries were reported.
Macy's postponed the annual Thanksgiving parade until Saturday because of concerns about how the parade's massive balloons would fare in the wind-swept canyons between Manhattan's skyscrapers.
A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, near Houston, said it raised a staggering $350,000 to allow its 500 members to stay in New York City for two extra nights.
"This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band for Pearland High School, told CBS News on Thursday.
Visitors who had traveled to New York to attend the parade were forced to make last-minute changes to their travel plans. Amanda Anderson, a Florida-based makeup artist who was hired to do makeup for parade performers, told CBS News New York she was able to rebook her flights so she could stay an extra day.
"I was in Macy's, actually, when I found out, and I look up and there was like three girls crying already," Anderson said when she learned the parade had been postponed. "People were sitting down, very somber. It was an experience."
Major roadways flooded, holiday travel disrupted
The storm flooded coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey as the high tide rolled in Thursday morning. Roads were closed and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.
Avalon, New Jersey, was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history, Borough of Avalon Business Administrator Scott J. Wahl said.
"Not quite Hurricane Sandy," Wahl said of the benchmark storm for his village on the far south of New Jersey's Atlantic coast.
Floodwaters washed debris over the road next to the shore, and a few drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades and into floodwaters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said.

title: 4 datos económicos que explican cómo llega España a las elecciones generales del 29N
rawText:
4 datos económicos que explican cómo llega España a las elecciones generales del 29N
  - Autor, Atahualpa Amerise
  - Título del autor, BBC News Mundo
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 8 min
España llega a las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre con una economía que crece a más del doble del ritmo de la eurozona y más trabajadores que nunca antes.
Muchas familias, sin embargo, apenas notan la mejoría: los salarios siguen muy por debajo de la media europea, mientras el costo de la vida no ha dejado de aumentar.
Quienes no poseen vivienda en propiedad se enfrentan, además, a los precios prohibitivos tanto de compra como de alquiler en el mercado inmobiliario español.
La distancia entre la marcha de la economía y lo que se percibe en el bolsillo está en el centro del debate entre los dos principales aspirantes a gobernar España.
El socialista Pedro Sánchez, que lleva más de ocho años al frente del gobierno, y sus socios más izquierdistas, Frente Amplio y Podemos, defienden políticas basadas en una mayor intervención del Estado en la economía, la redistribución de la riqueza y el refuerzo de la protección social.
El principal candidato opositor, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, líder del conservador Partido Popular, junto a Vox a su derecha, apuestan por reducir la carga fiscal, facilitar la actividad empresarial, promover la construcción de viviendas y dar más protagonismo a la iniciativa privada.
Analizamos cómo llega la economía de España a las elecciones a través de cuatro datos clave: la evolución del PIB, el empleo, los salarios y la pobreza infantil.
1. El PIB
Entre julio y septiembre de 2026, el producto interno bruto (PIB) de España creció un 2,7% respecto al mismo período del año anterior.
El crecimiento fue superior al del conjunto de la eurozona, del 1,3%, según Eurostat.
Durante la pandemia, España había sufrido una caída más profunda que la de sus vecinos: en el segundo trimestre de 2020, su economía se había contraído un 21,5% interanual frente al 13,8% en la eurozona.
Luego vino el rebote y, tras recuperar el terreno perdido, España siguió creciendo más deprisa.
Apuntalaron este crecimiento el consumo y la inversión dentro del país, que aportaron 2,6 puntos de la cifra del 2,7%.
También han influido los fondos que la Unión Europea destinó a la recuperación tras la pandemia, que explican entre el 10% y el 14% del crecimiento medio anual de la economía española entre 2021 y 2025, según un estudio del centro de análisis económico Funcas y la consultora Afi.
El gobierno también ha aumentado el endeudamiento público para financiar gastos y ayudas: en septiembre de 2026, la deuda pública era del 3,4% anual y equivalía al 100,3% del PIB, según el Banco de España.
En todo caso, hay un factor clave que explica el fuerte crecimiento del PIB: España tiene 2,5 millones de habitantes más que hace 5 años gracias a la llegada masiva de inmigrantes, que ha situado su población en torno a los 50 millones.
El aumento demográfico se ha traducido en un incremento de la población activa y, por tanto, de la actividad económica en términos absolutos.
"En términos per cápita España ya no sale tan bien en la foto de la eurozona", explica a BBC Mundo José García Montalvo, catedrático de Economía de la Universitat Pompeu Fabra, quien observa que, al dividir lo que produce el país entre más habitantes, el avance es menor.
Entre el segundo trimestre de 2019 (antes de la pandemia) y el mismo período de 2026, el PIB español en términos absolutos creció un 12,1%, frente al 7,8% de la eurozona, según Eurostat.
Sin embargo, al medir el PIB real por habitante, la ventaja española se redujo a medio punto: un 6% de crecimiento acumulado frente al 5,5% de la zona euro.
El crecimiento económico per cápita fue mayor en Lituania (16,8%), Letonia (12,7%), Eslovaquia (10,7%), Italia (9,2%) y Portugal (8,4%), entre otros.
2. El trabajo

title: Efecto BYD: por qué Brasil se ha convertido en un "laboratorio en América Latina" para las empresas chinas
rawText:
Efecto BYD: por qué Brasil se ha convertido en un "laboratorio en América Latina" para las empresas chinas
  - Autor, Camilla Veras Mota y Vitor Serrano
  - Título del autor, Enviados da BBC News Brasil a Camaçari y Salvador
- Fecha de publicación
- Tiempo de lectura: 10 min
A principios de 2026 circuló la información —falsa— de que Salvador de Bahía, en noreste de Brasil, estaba sufriendo una invasión china.
Videos compartidos en redes sociales mostraban la construcción de un complejo de alojamientos que, según la narrativa de la noticia falsa, se estaba levantando para albergar a 10.000 chinos que trabajarían en la recién inaugurada fábrica de BYD.
BYD es el fabricante chino de automóviles que superó a Tesla, de Elon Musk, en 2025, convirtiéndose en el mayor productor de vehículos eléctricos del mundo.
La empresa eligió Camaçari, en la región metropolitana de Salvador, para instalar su mayor planta en América Latina.
Aunque parte del proyecto sigue en construcción, la fábrica fue inaugurada en octubre de 2025. En menos de un año, de ella han salido más de 100.000 vehículos —ensamblados a partir de kits importados— que llegaron a concesionarios de todo el país, situando a la marca entre las más vendidas.
Está previsto que la producción made in Brasil comience a finales de 2026. Aun así, la planta ya cuenta con 7.618 empleados directos. De este total, el 6% (457) son extranjeros, según la compañía. La investigación periodística reveló que la gran mayoría son chinos.
Además, hay trabajadores chinos participando en las obras que se están llevando a cabo tanto en el complejo de la fábrica como en los bloques de alojamiento para el personal.
Según los registros de la Policía Federal, desde 2024 se han expedido 2.310 visados de residencia en Camaçari y en la vecina localidad de Lauro de Freitas; la mayoría de ellos son temporales.
"Ellos aman la libertad de Bahía"
Fin de Anuncio app
En una ciudad de poco más de 300.000 habitantes, la presencia china no es evidente. No existe una zona donde se concentren los recién llegados, una especie de "barrio chino" en Camaçari. Están dispersos entre hoteles y algunos complejos residenciales cerrados.
Tampoco hay una oleada de nuevos restaurantes gestionados por inmigrantes y orientados a su propia comunidad. Muchos empleados de BYD comen en la cantina de la propia fábrica —que cuenta con una sección de platos chinos y otra de recetas brasileñas— o en sus casas.
La percepción predominante es que trabajan mucho y salen poco.
"Nosotros [los brasileños] llegamos a casa, nos damos una ducha, nos tumbamos en el sofá, vemos la televisión... Ellos no; siguen trabajando incluso después de llegar a casa. Son muy reservados", comenta Cássia Cotia, una agente inmobiliaria que vive en un complejo residencial donde más de 60 viviendas están alquiladas a ciudadanos chinos.
Pero las características de este nuevo flujo migratorio se van revelando poco a poco.
En el mercado central de Camaçari —entre plátanos, camarones secos, café y tapioca— dos restaurantes que sirven "yakisoba" (plato popular de la cocina asiática) lucen ahora carteles con ideogramas chinos.
Por su parte, la comunidad local de los Testigos de Jehová ha comenzado recientemente a celebrar sus reuniones en mandarín.
Los "más desenvueltos", como los describe Cássia, se aventuran en los "forrós" (lugares donde se baila el género musical originario del noreste de Brasil) y en otros lugares de la vida nocturna de la ciudad, y no es raro que terminen apareciendo en las redes sociales.
Una escena que se hizo viral recientemente mostraba a una joven enseñándole a un hombre chino a mover las caderas, acompañada por el texto: "China va a adoctrinar a Brasil / Brasil adoctrinando a China".
Durante una visita a la ciudad, el equipo de BBC News Brasil se encontró con un grupo animado que bebía cerveza y comía pizza en una mesa sobre la acera, cerca de la Praça dos 46, uno de los lugares donde los habitantes de la ciudad se reúnen al final del día para pase

title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
rawText:
A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, according to reports from NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.
The Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.
In total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The company was acquitted of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. In a statement to NBC News, a Huawei spokesperson said the charges are “without legal or factual merit.” Huawei plans to appeal the decision and may face fines, forfeiture, and restitution, according to Bloomberg.
Huawei didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

title: Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
rawText:
Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
- Published
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.
United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.
Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.
"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.
"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.
"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"
United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.
They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.
It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.
Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.
There has been no apology from Webb on this occasion.
Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball."
United sources claim this interpretation is wrong.
The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.
This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.
Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.
"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.
"We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?"
Webb defends Yoro red card
What referee's chief Webb said about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.
"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.
"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.
"That if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.
"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and
"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong."

title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
rawText:
Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.
GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.
Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.
Some have managed to get the game to boot on PC, but recompiling the full game won’t be easy — even with help from AI tools like Claude. Take-Two is trying to slow this progress, and its IP enforcement team targeted the main GitHub repository for Leonida and more than 2,900 forks of it, claiming that it “infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.”
PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.
At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

title: Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record by scoring 204 off 53 balls
rawText:
Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record by scoring 204 off 53 balls
- Published
India's 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit the most sixes ever recorded in a senior men's innings in blazing 204 from 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates.
While almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi hit 28 sixes and seven fours in the Asia Cup Rising Stars competition - easily breaking Chad Bowes' previous record of 103 balls from 2024.
The teenage opener also broke the record for the fastest century and 150, the latter of which he already held, before being caught at long-off with his side five runs from victory.
India A ultimately passed their target of 250, played against a UAE side that featured a number of internationals but was not their current first-choice side, in 14.2 overs in Doha.
Sooryavanshi now holds the following records in List A cricket, the categorisation given to senior one-day matches:
- Fastest fifty: 11 balls v Sri Lanka A, 21 June (previously Kaushalya Weeraratne, 12 balls, 1 November 2005)
- Fastest hundred: 28 balls, today (previously Jake Fraser-McGurk, 29 balls, 8 October 2023)
- Fastest 150: 40 balls, today (previously himself, 59 balls, 24 December 2025)
- Fastest 200: 52 balls, today (previously Chad Bowes, 103 balls, 22 October 2024)
The previous record for the most sixes in senior matches was 26, struck by Tanmay Agarwal in an innings of 366 for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in India's first-class Ranji Trophy competition in January 2024.
The record in List A cricket was 23 sixes, struck by D'Arcy Short for Queensland in his 257 against Tasmania on 28 September 2018.
Sooryavanshi also holds the records of being the youngest century-maker in both List A and T20 cricket and the youngest captain in T20s.
"The first thing that's required in this format is being fearless, he's got plenty of that," former India batter Deep Dasgupta told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"Technically he's quite unique. There is a tendency of being over-coached in this generation, there's so many coaches and when you start playing franchise cricket.
"The best part is he has been fast-tracked so he hasn't had a lot of coaches, he's kind of untouched. What you see of him is predominantly what his natural game is.
"That bat swing, the hand speed, which is very, very natural and one of the quickest you'll come across. Technically he's very gifted, he's very special and he's definitely the real deal."
Sooryavanshi has rapidly become a sensation in T20 cricket since making his debut in the Indian Premier League in 2025 at the age of 14.
He has hit two hundreds and six fifties in his first two seasons in the competition and has earned 10 caps for India in the shortest format since making his debut against England in July.
The left-hander, who was batting in only his 16th List A innings in Doha and made his second century in the format, is yet to play for India in 50-over cricket.
He put on partnerships of 68 with opening partner Abhishek Sharma, who scored 12, 40 with Prabhsimran Singh, who added just three, and 137 with Rinku Singh, who scored an unbeaten 27.
The India A side, which featured a number of internationals, restricted the UAE to 249-8 in 50 overs, external after their opposition had chosen to bat and swiftly reached 254-3 to win by seven wickets and guarantee their place in the semi-finals.
The Rising Stars competition features A sides from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Afghanistan alongside squads from the UAE, Nepal and Hong Kong.
India A, who now top Group B, beat Nepal and lost to Pakistan A in their previous two matches in the competition, with Sooryavanshi making scores of 26 and 11.
Pakistan A will retake the top spot if they beat Nepal on Tuesday, with semi-finals on Thursday and Friday to follow before Sunday's final.

title: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
rawText:
What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
What it's like in the halls of a climate conference as it collapses
After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
ROB SCHMITZ, HOST:
International climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended today after negotiations fell apart. NPR's Rachel Waldholz has been at the conference and sent us this report.
RACHEL WALDHOLZ, BYLINE: I'm here in the Antalya Expo Center, which, for the past two weeks, has been packed with some 70,000 people who came to the COP31 climate conference. Now it's almost completely empty. In fact, they're disassembling parts of the venue around me. The climate talks ran two days past their scheduled end. By the time the gavel fell, many negotiators had already left to catch their flights home. Australia climate chief Chris Bowen led the negotiations.
CHRIS BOWEN: I haven't slept for the last three nights, been negotiating all the way through, but more importantly, people on delegations came at it and gave it everything they had.
WALDHOLZ: Delegates came to Antalya with long wish lists, from electrifying more of the global economy to money for developing countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change. Looming over it all is that this is the first summit to squarely face the reality that the planet will miss a key target of the Paris Climate Agreement, reaching warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above pre-Industrial levels. The U.N. says limiting that overshoot requires cutting the use of fossil fuels nearly in half in the next 10 to 15 years. Many countries wanted an agreement explicitly calling for a transition away from coal, oil and natural gas. But big oil-producing countries, like Saudi Arabia, blocked any mention of fossil fuels. Ultimately, the European Union decided no deal was better than the deal on the table. Darragh O'Brien is Ireland's environment minister.
DARRAGH O'BRIEN: We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.
WALDHOLZ: Many negotiators left the expo center dragging their suitcases on the way to the airport. They'll pick up negotiations next year at the next climate summit in Ethiopia. I'm Rachel Waldholz in Antalya, Turkey.

title: Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage
rawText:
All Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are facing significant delays on Sunday due to a problem with the system that calculates a plane’s weight and balance. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is Delta’s largest hub and one of the busiest airports in the world. While only Delta is impacted at the moment, disruptions at Hartsfield-Jackson could potentially affect other airports and airlines if delays continue to pile up.
Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage
Major delays for Delta come just a week after a nationwide groundstop.
The issues with Delta’s systems in Atlanta come just one week after an FAA outage led to a nationwide groundstop and thousands of canceled flights. According to The New York Times:
The system that went offline calculates the total weight of an airplane, including its airframe, fuel, passengers and their baggage. The system also allows pilots to determine the plane’s center of gravity and whether the weight is evenly distributed — data points that help ensure safe passage.
“Delta teams are using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” the airline said in a statement on Sunday.
